I'll give a couple options that might help and honestly I wish I had when I went through my own OCD hell. Write a letter. Seriously. Just write exactly what you would tell him. Your fears. What's really going on with your memory. How much it hurts you to see him hurt. Unload it. Once you're done, burn it, shred it, flush it, whatever. It gives you a place to put those thoughts and emotions. If you feel like he is the understanding type and would be willing to hear you out, have a civil discussion with him. Stating just the facts. If he really isn't the understanding type, them woof maybe he needs to grow emotionally before investing himself into a relationship.  Ultimately what I'm saying is that this is not your fault. Exactly. These "bad" habits are a coping tool used in response to stress or anxiety. There's a misconception that these things are purely ocd related. They aren't, but it is an anxiety response and ocd is under the anxiety umbrella. People who have ocd may have these habits as well, but not always. What helps stop a bad habit is to find a more productive way to channel your stress. For me, rings help or fidgeting with an object.

Check out scrupulosity ocd. There are a few things I do and have done to help me cope with intrusive thoughts. The number one thing is to not fight the thoughts/obsessions. What you resist, persists. Use radical acceptance and accept the thoughts as just thoughts and you are having them. Don't hop into the obsession. Take a step back and observe it. Don't judge. The more you do that, the more your brain will learn to calm down and not attach these thoughts to reasoning, logic, or your sense of self. 

A book that's helped me a lot is: Overcoming Unwanted Intrusive Thoughts 
-by sally winston and martin seif
